proposed_features.description: Identifies the core domain or subject matter the text is primarily about, which is often the most direct discriminator between categories.

Categorizes the nature of the event described—whether it's a regulatory decision, a corporate restructuring, a legal challenge, a natural disaster impact, a security update, a market movement, a sports outcome, or a political transition.
Reflects the immediacy or time-sensitivity of the event, ranging from real-time reporting to retrospective or future-oriented discussion.
Indicates the spatial scale of the event or subject—local, national, international, or global—often correlating with the category’s focus.
Identifies the type of institution or organization central to the narrative, such as government, corporation, legal system, or sports league.
Describes the point of view or framing of the text—whether it's objective reporting, personal commentary, or institutional announcement.
Measures the level of technical or specialized terminology used, which is higher in SciTech and Business and lower in Sports and World.

Indicates whether the text centers on individual people, groups, or abstract entities, with Sports and World often focusing on individuals, while Business and SciTech focus on organizations or systems.
Reflects whether the text emphasizes a result, a process, or a future possibility, with Sports and Business often emphasizing outcomes, while World and SciTech may focus on processes or developments.
Captures the emotional valence or intensity of the text, ranging from neutral to celebratory, critical, or urgent, which can vary by category.
Indicates whether the text includes specific numerical data, statistics, or financial figures, which is common in Business and SciTech but less so in Sports and World.
Identifies the target of the action described—whether it's a policy, a product, a person, or a system—helping distinguish between categories.
